item.title: Sundance Review: The Gallerist Is Too Referential to Properly Satirize the Art World
item.description: Taking on the art world is notoriously difficult—it’s already too ridiculous, and so the heightening of reality necessary for proper satire doesn’t work. There’s nowhere to go. item.title: Sundance Review: Wicker Audaciously Contemplates the Self-Destructive Perils of Jealousy
item.description: The jealousy of unhappy couples. The pettiness of mean girls. The frustration of insecure husbands. It’s a tale as old as time that’s curiously interpreted by writer-directors Eleanor Wilson and Alex Huston Fischer in Wicker, an audacious, captivating film about an outcast woman, her wood-woven husband, and the village that collapses over their love.
